approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 54 Chapter 736
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 1741-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend the insurance law, in relation to calculating an
        insured individual's overall contribution to  any  out-of-pocket
        maximum or any cost-sharing requirement"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  requires  insurance  companies  to  apply  price reduction
instruments to any out-of-pocket expenses when  calculating  an  insured
individual's  cost-sharing  requirement.  These  coupons could reduce or
even eliminate copays, deductibles, or other patient costs when  filling
a  prescription  at  the pharmacy. These coupons are also issued by drug
manufacturers as a tool to encourage consumers to use their  brand  name
drugs,  which often are a higher cost to the State and private insurance
payors.
 
  New Yorkers are struggling with the cost of living, and I support  all
worthy  efforts  to reduce costs and keep money in New Yorkers' pockets.
While this legislation is well-intentioned, as-written it could have the
effect of pushing consumers to purchase more expensive brand-name  drugs
rather  than  less  expensive,  equally effective, generic alternatives.
Medicaid and other insurance plans have policies in  place  that  ensure
patients  receive  the lowest cost equivalent drug to address this exact
issue.
 
  I have reached an  agreement  with  the  Legislature  to  limit  these
coupons  to  brand  name drugs that do not have a generic equivalent and
brand name drugs for which the patient has received authorization.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Requires any third-party payments, financial assistance, discount, voucher or other price reduction instrument for out-of-pocket expenses made on behalf of an insured individual for the cost of prescription drugs to be applied to the insured's deductible, copayment, coinsurance, out-of-pocket maximum, or any other cost-sharing requirement when calculating such insured individual's overall contribution to any out-of-pocket maximum or any cost-sharing requirement.
